saints.name: St. Camillus de Lellis
saints.title: Priest and Founder
saints.shortBlurb: A former soldier and gambler who founded an order to serve the sick and dying…
biography: Born at Bucchianico in the Abruzzi in 1550, the son of a soldier, Camillus lost his mother young and soldiered for Venice and Naples until 1574. A compulsive gambler, he campaigned against the Turks and suffered abscessed feet that never healed.

A sermon of the Capuchin guardian at Manfredonia converted him; admitted among the Capuchins, he was dismissed for that same infirmity. In Rome's Hospital for Incurables, San Giacomo, he rose from nurse to director and, guided by St. Philip Neri, was ordained priest in 1584.

He founded the Clerks Regular, Ministers of the Infirm — the Camillians, known by the red cross on their habit — vowed to serve the sick even at risk of life. Approved by Sixtus V in 1586 and raised to a religious order by Gregory XIV in 1591, the order lost two companions nursing a plague fleet off Naples, its first 'martyrs of charity.'

He resigned the generalship in 1607 to tend the sick and died at Rome on 14 July 1614. Beatified in 1742 and canonized in 1746 by Benedict XIV, he was named by Pius XI in 1930, with St. John of God, patron of the sick, of hospitals, and of nurses.
saints.knownFor: Founding the Camillians and the compassionate care of the sick.
